family.tagline: Eight clients, two kids and one dog, kept in order.
family.story: Folake keeps the books for eight small clients from the Den. Tobias teaches secondary school and marks at the dining table. Bayo, Hanna and the dog keep the house loud.

companion.name: Tamar
companion.job: Drafts monthly client summaries from the notes Folake texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Folake sends every summary.

companion.name: Fenn
companion.job: Opens Vikunja in its own browser and files the term's marking tasks.
companion.limits: Adds tasks Tobias names. He ticks them off.

popup.title: A parcel on the porch
popup.body: A parcel waits on the porch. Tobias carries it through the foyer to the living room, with the dog supervising.

popup.title: Hanna reads the packing list
popup.body: Hanna reads the list: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Its footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Folake plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Tobias joins from his phone
popup.body: Between two piles of marking, Tobias joins the Core's own network from his phone. Then he picks the home network.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Folake picks Hermes and Companion Memory (beta). Tobias picks OpenClaw. Together they add Paperless-ngx, Vikunja and Immich, then walk away.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Tamar says hello
popup.body: Folake messages the agent she named Tamar. Tamar answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: folake
say.text: Hello, Folake. Tamar here. Where shall we start?

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Weekend photos, backed up
popup.body: Tobias backs up the weekend's photos to Immich from the couch. The dog in the leaves and Hanna's sandcastle land on the Core, ready to search.

beats.capability: a small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: Parents' evening meets client calls
popup.body: By the fire, Tobias adds the school term dates to Baikal. Folake's phone reads the same calendar, so parents' evening and client calls sit side by side.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: One filter for the whole house
popup.body: Tobias opens Pi-hole beside the Core. It blocks ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level for every phone and laptop on the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: turn a folder of photos and videos into a private feed with albums and a timeline

popup.title: Summer, scrolling past on the TV
popup.body: Friday is photo night. Foldergram turns the summer folder into a private feed on the family-room TV, and Hanna calls out every picture.

beats.capability: run a quiz night for a small group on your own Core

popup.title: Bayo runs the quiz night
popup.body: Bayo writes the questions for Friday's family quiz and runs the night in Razzia. Everyone answers from the beanbags, and the dog gets no vote.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses, with a recipe book

popup.title: Mother's jollof rice, written once
popup.body: Folake types her mother's jollof rice into the HomeHub recipe book. Tobias adds the ingredients to the shared shopping list from his phone.

beats.capability: track accounts, budgets, bills and savings goals, with rules that sort your transactions

popup.title: The month, sorted by rules
popup.body: Folake imports the household's month from a bank CSV into Firefly III. Its rules sort each transaction, and the totals stay on the Core.

beats.capability: assign and track household chores and recurring tasks, with NFC tag completion

popup.title: A tag by the dog's bowl
popup.body: Bayo taps his phone on the tag by the dog's bowl. Donetick marks dinner done, and Tobias sees the tick.

beats.capability: lists, boards and calendars for tasks, with reminders and recurring jobs

popup.title: Fenn adds the marking tasks
popup.body: Tobias reads out the term's marking deadlines. Fenn opens Vikunja in its own browser and adds each one. Tobias ticks them off himself.

say.speaker: tobias
say.text: Tasks added. Please check the list.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: A carrier bag of receipts
popup.body: A client hands Folake a carrier bag of receipts. She scans them into Paperless-ngx, which reads every page, tags it and makes the lot searchable.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Tamar drafts the month's summary
popup.body: Folake texts Tamar her notes on a client's month. Tamar drafts the summary from the context Folake connected to Companion Memory. Folake reads it and sends it herself.

say.speaker: folake
say.text: Draft ready. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Hours per client, in one place
popup.body: Folake starts a timer in Kimai for each of her eight clients. At month end the report for every one is waiting.

beats.capability: a PDF toolkit that runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded

popup.title: Statements merged into one file
popup.body: At month end Folake merges a client's statements into one PDF with BentoPDF. It runs in her browser, and nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: keeps your digital life on your own disk, so your agents know your context

popup.title: Folake chooses what to connect
popup.body: Folake picks which client notes go into Companion Memory, a file on the Core's disk. The rest stay out, and she can disconnect it whenever she likes.

beats.capability: a shared whiteboard on an infinite canvas

popup.title: One canvas for two artists
popup.body: Hanna and Bayo share one tldraw canvas at the kids' desk. She draws the dog, and he adds the speech bubble.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: A chapter before lights out
popup.body: Bayo reads his current novel in Koodo Reader from the bunk bed. His place and highlights stay in the library on the Core.

beats.capability: log workouts: sets, reps, weights, distances and personal records

popup.title: Lengths logged by the pool
popup.body: Tobias swims before breakfast and logs the distance in Wingfit on the pool terrace. His personal records sit in one list on the Core.

beats.capability: plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: Sunday's dog walk, mapped
popup.body: On Sunday morning Folake plans the dog walk in Wanderer. She loads a GPX file, and the saved route lives on the Core.

popup.title: Four people, one dog, one Core
popup.body: A bookkeeper, a teacher, two children and a dog. The Oyelaran-Brandt household runs on one Companion Core in the living room.

closing.body: Your receipts, your calendar and your carrier bags can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one scan in Paperless-ngx.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
Client ledgers care note: the Den beats say the files sit on the Core and make no compliance, tax or accuracy claim. Folake sends every summary herself.
kitchen-dog uses Donetick's NFC tag completion for the iot category. The catalog caveat says Donetick notifications use Telegram or Pushover; the text claims neither.
kitchen-month: bank CSV import only (catalog caveat: bank sync goes through outside providers). Firefly III is a bookkeeping tool: no advice, no savings promise.
den-pdf and den-carrier-bag: BentoPDF "nothing is uploaded" and Paperless-ngx OCR are copied from the catalog listings. Paperless-ngx AI features are off by default and unused.
Mealie was not used (no QA screenshot); HomeHub carries the recipe book. Jellyfin was left out for fleet spread. The dog is a pet: no pet app is claimed.
Voice-over lexicon: Oyelaran, Folake, Tobias, Bayo, Hanna, Tamar, Fenn, Netherwick, Bramblecott, Foldergram, Razzia, Kimai, BentoPDF, Wingfit, Wanderer, tldraw, Donetick, Vikunja.
Street Bramblecott Road and town Netherwick are invented; the human map check is still open.
